notes.lines: Every precinct line is the Bureau of Elections', generalised by at most 1.5 metres and set on a grid of 0.00001 degree (about a metre); where two neighbours' drawings of one line lay within 1 metre of each other they were made one line. The state, counties, cities and townships, wards and district courts are put together from whole precincts. A point within a few metres of a line can fall on either side of it. The precincts stop at the Great Lakes and the rivers between them.
notes.districts: Which House, Senate, congressional and county commissioner district a precinct lies in is worked out here by laying the State's district lines over the precinct (analysis, not an official list). Where such a line runs through a precinct (a second district holds 3% of it or more, in a part at least 60 metres thick) the precinct is cut along the line and each piece is a shape of its own (id <precinct>.<n>, the Bureau's id under 'precinct'), so a point is given the districts of its own piece. A precinct that could not be cut carries 'split' and is listed under check. Near any district line the Michigan Voter Information Center decides.
notes.places: A precinct belongs to one city or township (the precinct table says which). A village lies inside a township, and a voter in a village is a voter of the township too; a precinct that reaches into a village lists it (mcd_all), and the mcd layer answers for a point, villages first: a point inside a village's limits is given the village, and it is in the township around it too.
notes.judicial: A district court district, or the election division of one, is a group of counties, cities and townships set out in the Revised Judicature Act (MCL 600.8101 to 600.8163). Where the act keeps two versions of a district side by side, the one with a seat on the Bureau of Elections' 2026 candidate listing is taken as in force; where neither is listed the precinct is given no district. Circuit judges are elected by the counties of the circuit (the precinct's circuit), probate judges by the county.
notes.commissioners: County commissioner districts are the 2021 apportionment as the State compiled it; a county that has redrawn its districts since is not known here.
notes.school: School district lines are the Michigan Geographic Framework's. Which districts a precinct lies in is analysis, not an official list: a district counts when its part of the precinct is at least 60 metres thick somewhere; school_pct is each district's share of the precinct's area (land and water, not voters).
notes.authority: For which precinct an address votes in, and where, the Michigan Voter Information Center (the Department of State) and the city or township clerk are the authority.
notes.precinct_ids: A precinct's id is the Bureau of Elections' own: WP, the county's three-digit code, the city's or township's five-digit Census code, and the two-digit ward and three-digit precinct numbers. A piece of a split precinct adds a full stop and its number.

format.files: Every file is TopoJSON on one grid (transform above): arcs are delta-encoded lines; a shape's arcs name the lines of its rings, a negative number n meaning line ~n backwards; outer rings run counter-clockwise, holes clockwise.
format.county_files: precincts/<county>.json, object 'precincts': one shape per precinct, id = the Bureau's precinct id. arcMask[i] has bit k set when line i is an outline of arc_kinds[k]; arcSides[2i] and arcSides[2i+1] are the precincts on the right and left of line i (-1: a precinct in another county's file, -2: no precinct: the state's edge, a Great Lake, or a gap between two drawings); names gives the names of the places the file's precincts lie in.
format.boxes: boxes[county] holds four whole numbers a precinct, in the file's order: west, south, east, north in steps of box_step degrees from the transform's translate, rounded outwards. A point is tried against every precinct whose box (widened by half a step) holds it.

precinct_properties.name: the precinct's name (City of Holland, Ward 4, Precinct 7)
precinct_properties.mcd_all: list, when the precinct reaches into a village: its city or township, then the villages, largest share first
precinct_properties.mcd_pct: list, with mcd_all: the share of the precinct's area in each, in percent (a village lies inside the township)
precinct_properties.ward: list: the council districts the precinct lies in (absent where the city has no wards)
precinct_properties.com: county commissioner district holding most of the precinct
precinct_properties.house: state House district holding most of the precinct
precinct_properties.senate: state Senate district holding most of the precinct
precinct_properties.cd: congressional district holding most of the precinct
precinct_properties.judicial: district court (the district, or its election division, that elects the precinct's district judges; absent where the act offers two and neither is listed)
precinct_properties.circuit: judicial circuit (its circuit judges are elected by the counties of the circuit)
precinct_properties.precinct: the Bureau of Elections' precinct id (the shape's own id, but for a piece of a split precinct)
precinct_properties.parts: only on a piece of a split precinct: how many pieces the precinct was cut into along district lines
precinct_properties.split: only where a district line runs through the precinct and it could not be cut: for house, senate, cd or com, each district's share in percent
precinct_properties.school: list: the school districts the precinct lies in, largest share first
precinct_properties.school_pct: list, when the precinct is split: each district's share of its area, in percent
precinct_properties.school_out: percent of the precinct's area that lies in no school district (given from 3 percent up)
precinct_properties.school_edge: list: neighbouring districts that only brush the precinct along a line (try them too when placing a point)
precinct_properties.c: a point inside the precinct's largest part, for a label: [longitude, latitude]

ids.every layer: a shape's properties j and d are the jurisdiction id and the district its races carry on the ballot pages
ids.mcd: MI-M- and the Census code: a city's or township's county subdivision code (MI-M-22000), a village's place code; properties.t says city, township or village
ids.ward: <city>|<ward as the council race words it> (MI-M-34000|Ward 1)
ids.cd: the district (7); properties.race is the race for Congress
ids.judicial: MI-DC and the district court district, with its election division where judges are elected by division (MI-DC36, MI-DC52-1)
ids.school: MI-S- and the district's five-digit code (MI-S-33020)
